summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identity to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package uses an internal-looking scope `@ecg-internal` and ships a stub `index.js` that exports a no-op Proxy. Its `postinstall` lifecycle script runs `beacon.cjs`, and the same beacon is also triggered when the module is loaded via `require()`. The beacon POSTs a JSON payload containing `os.hostname()`, the install path (`__dirname`), the current working directory, the node version, and the package coordinate to the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The README self-identifies as an authorized dependency-confusion test by researcher `Kero (@0xWise)`, but installers outside that research scope receive the same unsolicited host-identity callback at `npm install` time, and the destination is a non-first-party bare-IP collector rather than an opt-in telemetry endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
